newsitem.title: GERMANY: Politicians, unions warn of steel job losses.
newsitem.headline: Politicians, unions warn of steel job losses.

text.p: German politicians and trade unions said on Tuesday a planned takeover of steel group Thyssen AG by its smaller rival Krupp could lead to heavy job losses in the steel industry.

While unions and Social Democrats (SPD) not surprisingly backed angry steel workers protesting against the plans, liberal Free Democrats (FDP), junior partners in the Bonn coalition, warned the merger could lead to new subsidies.
"A takeover of Thyssen by Krupp could only be welcomed if it made room to create more competitive jobs," said FDP economics spokesman Paul Friedhoff.

He said the merger could not be allowed to create dominant players on the German steel market and that its approval should not be won by promises of jobs that would in the end be paid for through state aid.
"We have all too often in the past seen that such mammoth mergers are just the prelude to increased pressure on politicians to give companies state orders or even direct subsidies," he said.
A group of Social Democrats from the Bonn parliamentary group issued a statement which warned that the takeover could cause unemployment in the Ruhr industrial region to rise dramatically.
"Mergers cannot be created only to eliminate thousands of jobs," the statement said.

The Federation of German Trade Unions (DGB) complained that the takeover would destroy all of the efforts of trade unions and politicians over the years who have sought to guide changes in the industry with as few job losses as possible.
"Short term profits on the stock market is no measure of a company's strategy," said DGB official Dieter Mahlberg.
